rationale: The method replaces '&', '<', '>', '"', and '\'' with HTML entity references, so the value cannot open a tag or attribute boundary in HTML content or in a quoted HTML attribute, and the same references are well-formed in XML content and quoted XML attributes. Space and CR/LF pass through raw, so the attribute claim assumes a quoted attribute value and the value is not single-line for log. It encodes nothing for any other named context.

rationale: This is the encode(String, String) overload with a charset name; the Charset overload behaves identically. The method percent-encodes every character that is illegal or has any reserved meaning anywhere in a URI per RFC 3986, so the output is the unreserved alphabet plus %XX sequences and can contain no URI delimiter, quote, angle bracket, ampersand, parenthesis, backslash, whitespace, or control character; the value cannot break out of any quoted or delimited context in the neutralized list. The only gap is path: '..' sequences are legal URI characters and survive unchanged, so the value can still express parent-directory traversal.

rationale: This is the encodePath(String, String) overload; the Charset overload behaves identically. The method percent-encodes characters that are illegal within a URI path, including '?' and '#', so the value cannot escape the path portion of a URI into the query or fragment, and no raw control characters survive. The claim is only partial for url: '/' and the path sub-delimiters (including ';', '=', '&', and quotes) survive by design, so the value can add path segments and matrix parameters, and '..' sequences survive, so the value is not safe for path.

rationale: This is the encodePathSegment(String, String) overload; the Charset overload behaves identically. The method percent-encodes every character that is illegal in one URI path segment, including '/', '?', and '#', so the value cannot add path segments and cannot escape into the query or fragment, and no raw control characters survive. The claim is only partial for url: the RFC 3986 pchar sub-delimiters (including ';', '=', '&', and the single quote) survive by design, so matrix-parameter injection within the segment remains possible, and '..' sequences survive, so the value is not safe for path and not safe in any context whose metacharacters include the surviving sub-delimiters.
